Which Oil Seal Material Do I Need?

Ethylene acrylic elastomer. Our signature compound for rotary sealing, supplied to Mahindra & Mahindra for transmission applications. Holds compression-set stability where oil, heat and ozone act together.
Fluorocarbon rubber, the first choice for aggressive chemistry and sustained heat. Resists petroleum oils, fuels and many solvents where nitrile is attacked.
Nitrile butadiene rubber, the general-purpose standard for oil sealing. Outstanding resistance to petroleum oils and hydraulic fluids at moderate temperature.
Water, steam and brake fluid service, with excellent weather and ozone resistance. Not for petroleum oils — the commonest mis-specification on a seal.

The widest service range of the eight, for high-temperature static sealing. Biocompatible grades available; we do not hold FDA registration or ISO 13485. Poor abrasion resistance — not for a rotating shaft.
Balanced properties across weather, refrigerants and moderate oil. Flame-retardant grades available. Rarely specified for rotary service.
Abrasion resistance at low cost, for static seals in water and mild service. Not for oil or fuel contact, and rarely specified for rotary service.
The highest resilience of the eight, specified where a seal also has to damp. Not for oil, fuel or sustained heat, and rarely specified for rotary service.
